brands.d: Rochester, NY knitting mill that made the first hooded sweatshirt and patented Reverse Weave cross-grain construction in 1938; now owned by Authentic Brands.
Manhattan skate shop and label founded by James Jebbia whose red Futura box logo, weekly drops and collaborations made it the most influential streetwear brand.
Ura-Harajuku streetwear brand founded by Nigo, known for ape-head camo, the Bapesta and the Shark hoodie; now owned by I.T Group, Hong Kong.
Alexander City, Alabama mill that originated the cotton sweatshirt in the late 1920s; now a Fruit of the Loom brand.
eras: Fruit of the Loom / Berkshire Hathaway, 2006–

brands.d: World's largest athletic footwear and apparel company, whose Nike Sportswear Tech Pack introduced Tech Fleece in 2013.
Tokyo sweatshirt brand founded by Satoshi Suzuki that uses only tsuriami (loop-wheel) fabric knitted in Wakayama to keep the craft alive.
Japanese reproduction label best known for flight jackets, also making loop-wheeled 1930s–40s pattern sweatshirts and zip hoodies.
Family-run Norristown, Pennsylvania maker of very heavy cross-knit jersey sweatshirts and tees, originally for construction trades.
London brand by Nick and Steve Tidball making experimental garments such as the 100 Year Hoodie and Relaxation Hoodie.
Winston-Salem basics brand (Hanesbrands) selling EcoSmart fleece hoodies and sweatshirts at mass-market prices.
Montreal manufacturer of undecorated blank hoodies, fleeces and tees that are printed by others; the default blank hoodie.
Dearborn, Michigan family-owned workwear company whose heavyweight Marquette and K288 logo sweatshirts crossed into streetwear.

traditions.p: Early 20th century machines; revived from the 1990s
traditions.d: Knitting of sweatshirt jersey on slow vintage loop-wheel (tsuriami) machines that hang the fabric and knit without tension, about one metre of tubular cloth per hour.
traditions.tech: Loop-wheel circular knitting without tension; tubular, side-seamless body
traditions.auth: No side seams on the body, dense soft hand, Wakayama or Japan origin label; weight stated in oz or gsm

notes: Shelf rebuilt from 2 kinds / 23 flat models into 2 kinds with 7 (Hoodie) and 4 (Sweatshirt) archetypes plus short leftover model lists. Dropped: Carhartt FR Force Marquette (flame-resistant trade PPE, out of scope), AS Colour Stencil hoodies (wholesale blanks), Castore Garcia Hoody, Mondetta Flag Shirt, American Vintage Jitbay/Uscow (SKU noise, no archetype). Carhartt Marquette kept as a single leftover model per style. Champion Reverse Weave and BAPE Shark moved from flat models to archetypes with versions; Loopwheel added as a maker-group archetype (Loopwheeler originator, Buzz Rickson's and Real McCoy's versions) with a tradition entry. The Real McCoy's has no retrieved brand page, so its version carries an empty mk and no register entry. Buzz Rickson's and Camber official sites could not be fetched; retailer/distributor pages used and founding year left blank for Buzz Rickson's. Supreme Box Logo hoodie dated to seasonal releases only (no confirmed first-hoodie year). Nike Tech Fleece added as a hoodie archetype a knowledgeable buyer would expect. Weight types given in gsm/oz as attributes, not kinds. Uniqlo retail URL from old data replaced by Wikipedia kind pages.
